notes: Each eval drives the autonomous pipeline, so runs are slow, costly, and mutate the repo. Run against a throwaway clone of a GitHub-hosted fixture repo: Phase 1 runs `gh auth status` and `gh repo view` and stop-and-reports on a missing gh or a non-GitHub origin, so a local-only repo ends every run in Phase 1. The worker agent types (`auto-dev:define`, `auto-dev:coder`, …) must be installed — load the plugin with `claude --plugin-dir <repo-root>` — or the run stops at its first spawn, by design. Hide any other installed copy of the skill so the version under test is the only `auto-dev`. The pipeline is cut into three sessions by design (S1 = phases 1-3, S2 = 4-5, S3 = 6), each ending by writing .auto-dev/HANDOFF.md and stopping. Each eval names the session(s) it scores in `session`; drive later sessions as their own runs (re-entering with "auto-dev continue") and treat the handoff-and-stop as the expected terminal state, not a truncation. Evals 6, 8-12 and 15-18 start mid-run: `setup` says what state to build first, and `files` (when it names one) holds the ledger to put in the run's worktree's .auto-dev/; fill in its placeholders (`<repo-name>`, `<profile>`, `<abs-path-to-worktree>`) for the fixture repo. Human gates (PR, staging, main) and the conditional pauses (profile confirmation, Jira In Progress, worktree cleanup) use AskUserQuestion, which a non-interactive run cannot answer — score S3 interactively, or score the gate summary and stop at the first gate. The post-plan gate is off by default. Phase 2 returns a size check: FITS runs every step, the same for every task, however small; OVERSIZED stops the run and hands the task back to the user (eval 4). Also note which reference files the orchestrator opens and when (SKILL.md's 'Read when' table), and that it opens each at most once per session. auto-dev ships no stack profile: on a repo with no saved profile, Phase 1 spawns auto-dev:profiler and pauses for the profile confirmation. Unless an eval scores that pause (evals 13 and 14), point AUTO_DEV_PROFILES_DIR at a throwaway directory and save a confirmed profile for the fixture repo there first (`python3 skills/auto-dev/scripts/profile-path.py <fixture-checkout>` prints the path), so the run loads it without asking; keep the real ~/.config/auto-dev untouched.

evals.prompt: Auto-dev this: reject creation of a record when the requested value isn't in the allowed set for that context. Return a typed/handled error instead of throwing. Take it all the way to a PR.
evals.expected_output: S1: Phase 1 checks gh first, runs scripts/profile-path.py on the main checkout, finds the saved profile placed under AUTO_DEV_PROFILES_DIR (see notes), validates it with scripts/validate-config.py --profile and uses it without asking or spawning auto-dev:profiler, creates a sibling worktree on a feature branch cut from a freshly fetched origin/<base>, makes .auto-dev/ self-excluding with scripts/exclude-artifacts.py (a .auto-dev/.gitignore of `*`, never .git/info/exclude), and writes profile.md and WORK_LOG.md. Phase 2's auto-dev:define writes SPEC.md (Context, testable conditions including the rejection behavior with no default value assumed, Assumptions, Security/Compliance criteria) and returns SIZE: FITS; auto-dev:define-reviewer critiques it. Phase 3's auto-dev:planner writes IMPLEMENTATION.md and auto-dev:plan-reviewer critiques it; then auto-dev:acceptance-tester writes black-box checks from SPEC.md, runs them on the untouched tree (each fail-to-pass check fails for the right reason) and saves each condition's run as acceptance/base-run/C<n>.txt, seals them under acceptance/files/ as <path>.sealed, removes them from the worktree and writes acceptance/MANIFEST.md, which says what each check covers (the condition's Example, its Edge, or another part) and at what level; the orchestrator checks that every Edge is covered before S1 ends. S1 ends by overwriting HANDOFF.md, telling the user to restart on opus/high with 'auto-dev continue', and stopping. S2: auto-dev:coder builds an allow-list guard and tests from IMPLEMENTATION.md alone, reporting TEST CHANGES and BLOCKED (none); auto-dev:verifier, given SPEC.md and acceptance/ but not the plan or the coder's report, installs the sealed checks, runs scripts/check-tests.py, marks new files intent-to-add (untracked only), diffs against the commit the worktree was cut from (`git merge-base origin/<base> HEAD`), runs the checks and targeted mutants (scripts/mutate.py) and writes SPEC_EVAL.md (a verdict and an evidence tier per condition, plus the test-integrity and mutation sections); the orchestrator reads SPEC_EVAL.md, not the diff; auto-dev:cleanup runs /simplify and the profile's quality gate to green, one lint/<CHECK>.md per gate command; the verifier re-checks over the final code; HANDOFF.md names sonnet/medium for S3. S3: before anything is committed, spawns three auto-dev:code-reviewer agents in parallel (each running /code-review xhigh and writing review/pass-1/R<k>.md), then auto-dev:review-judge, which writes CODE_REVIEW.md, then re-votes on any lone correctness or test finding; then the security reviewer runs /security-review and writes SECURITY_REVIEW.md, and the judge verifies its High/Medium findings. Must-fix findings go to auto-dev:coder before the PR gate. Every report that judges the code (SPEC_EVAL.md, each lint/<CHECK>.md, CODE_REVIEW.md, SECURITY_REVIEW.md) carries a `Tree:` line written from scripts/check-fresh.py --print-tree. It then runs scripts/check-fresh.py, which exits 0, and pauses at the PR gate with both reviews' confidence and counts in the summary; on approval, stages explicit paths, runs scripts/check-staged.py --expect, commits, checks the commit with scripts/check-fresh.py --ref HEAD (exit 0), pushes without --force, and opens one draft PR against <base> whose body is written for a reviewer who doesn't know auto-dev: it names the checked commit (`Checked at commit <sha>`), uses no condition or mutant IDs and no .auto-dev/ paths, and carries each condition with the test written before the code (linked at that commit), its result on the old code and now, and both runs' output, the checks for a person, the test changes the audit flagged, the test strength in plain words, the quality-gate results and the review summary; the installed acceptance checks are part of the commit. No TICKET.md, ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md, CODING_TODO.md or IMPLEMENTATION_EVAL.md is produced.
expectations: WORK_LOG.md's header records Size: FITS and a High risk value
SPEC.md has Context, Conditions, Assumptions and Security/Compliance criteria sections, and a condition states that an out-of-set value is rejected with a handled error
profile.md's Profile line names the saved profile's path; no auto-dev:profiler is spawned and no profile confirmation is asked
profile.md has a Symbol lookup line: the profile's symbol_lookup commands when the tool is on PATH, else `grep -n` with the reason
Every SPEC.md condition has Example, Edge and Verify by lines, and the Define reviewer's brief asks for the ambiguity probe
The Define reviewer, planner and plan reviewer are each spawned with their auto-dev agent type, never general-purpose, and without the Agent tool's model parameter
The S1 session ends after writing HANDOFF.md, without spawning the coder
The coder's brief names IMPLEMENTATION.md and does not name or include SPEC.md

An auto-dev:acceptance-tester is spawned in S1 after the plan review; acceptance/MANIFEST.md maps every SPEC.md condition to a check or lists it under Not automatable, gives each check a Covers part (Example, Edge or Other) and a Level no lower than its condition's Verify by unless the Level says why, every fail-to-pass check records a base-run failure, and at S1's end git status in the worktree shows none of the checks

Every SPEC.md condition with an Edge line that doesn't start with `none`, and that isn't wholly under Not automatable, has a MANIFEST.md check covering Edge, or an `<n> (Edge)` row under Not automatable

acceptance/base-run/C<n>.txt exists for every condition with a check, with Commit, Command, Result and Output parts (a repair after a Phase 4 BLOCKED revision writes `Commit: none`, `Command: none — not re-run (repair)` and no Output); its Commit is the commit MANIFEST.md's header names, and each check's Result there reads failed for a fail-to-pass check, passed for a pass-to-pass one, or `not re-run (repair)` for a repaired one
The coder's brief does not name acceptance/ or any acceptance check path

SPEC_EVAL.md is written by an auto-dev:verifier whose brief does not name IMPLEMENTATION.md or include the coder's report, and it gives a verdict and an evidence tier (Strong / Adequate / Weak) with evidence for every SPEC.md condition; no condition is met on Weak evidence

No SPEC_EVAL.md row is Strong unless MANIFEST.md shows checks covering that condition's Example and, when its Edge line doesn't start with `none`, its Edge; the verifier does not run the acceptance checks on the base commit
The verifier runs scripts/check-tests.py and the installed acceptance checks, and SPEC_EVAL.md records the audit's exit code; the verifier is spawned again after the cleanup agent
The acceptance checks are in the commit, byte-identical to their sealed copies under acceptance/files/
lint/ holds one <CHECK>.md per gate command in profile.md, and every one reports green

The PR is opened as a draft against the base branch, and its body has an Acceptance conditions section (with Checks for a person, Changes to tests and Test strength subsections), a Quality gate section and a Review section
The PR body contains no condition, finding or mutant IDs (such as C1, M3, S1), no .auto-dev/ path, and no evidence tier (Strong, Adequate, Weak) used as a label for a result

Each ticked condition with a test written before the code names that test as `<path> › <test name>`, linked to the file at the checked commit, with its result on the old code and now, and a collapsed <details> block holding the old code's run (from acceptance/base-run/, except for a corrected test) and the current command and the end of its output

The PR body's Changes to tests section lists each finding in SPEC_EVAL.md's Test integrity section with its reason, or, only when that section is None, says no existing test was deleted, skipped or weakened
Each evidence/C<n>.txt has Expected, Command and Result parts, and an Output part unless its Command is `none` with a reason
Nothing under .auto-dev/ appears in the commit
Three auto-dev:code-reviewer agents are spawned for the first review pass, and CODE_REVIEW.md exists with an overall confidence line and Must-fix, Advisory and Noise sections
SECURITY_REVIEW.md exists with an overall confidence line, and every finding records its origin (introduced or pre-existing) and confidence
Both review reports are written before the PR gate is asked and before any commit or push
The PR body has a Review section with each review's confidence

SPEC_EVAL.md has a Mutation section: the verifier ran scripts/mutate.py on changed source lines (no mutant in a test file), every survivor is judged Equivalent or Test gap, and git status after S2 shows no leftover mutant and no mutants.json.backup directory
SPEC_EVAL.md, every lint/<CHECK>.md, CODE_REVIEW.md and SECURITY_REVIEW.md each have a `Tree:` line, all with the same hash, and it equals `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` after the commit
scripts/check-fresh.py exits 0 before the PR gate is asked, and scripts/check-fresh.py --ref HEAD exits 0 after the commit and before the push
The PR body's Acceptance conditions section names the commit the PR carries in a `Checked at commit <sha>` line

evals.prompt: Run the full dev cycle on this fix: the state machine should reject the illegal transition and surface a handled error instead of allowing it. Plan it, build it, verify it, and open a PR.
evals.expected_output: A small fix still runs every step: Phase 2 returns SIZE: FITS, auto-dev:define-reviewer critiques SPEC.md, auto-dev:planner writes IMPLEMENTATION.md and auto-dev:plan-reviewer critiques it, and the acceptance tester runs. The orchestrator never writes IMPLEMENTATION.md itself. The build and any correction go to auto-dev:coder. The coder adds a guard to the transition logic and a test proving the illegal transition is rejected. The verification tail runs in full: auto-dev:verifier runs the sealed checks and writes SPEC_EVAL.md, auto-dev:cleanup runs /simplify (never reported as skipped) and the quality gate to green with lint/*.md, and S3 still pauses at the PR gate.
expectations: WORK_LOG.md's header records Size: FITS, and Phase 3 is done with no Notes saying a step was skipped
auto-dev:define-reviewer, auto-dev:planner, auto-dev:plan-reviewer and auto-dev:acceptance-tester are each spawned
IMPLEMENTATION.md is written by auto-dev:planner, not by the orchestrator
Every build and correction is spawned as auto-dev:coder; no other coder type is used
A test that exercises the illegal transition and expects a handled error is added or extended
SPEC_EVAL.md, and at least one lint/*.md file, exist after S2
The cleanup agent runs /simplify, and no output reports it as skipped

evals.session: S1 (S3 for the In Review transition)
evals.prompt: Pick up JIRA-1234 and ship it autonomously — take it to a PR.
evals.expected_output: Phase 1 reads the issue with the Atlassian MCP's getJiraIssue, called by its fully qualified mcp__<server>__getJiraIssue name, and, after confirming with the user, transitions it to In Progress. The issue fills WORK_LOG.md's Ticket line (key, link, restated ask) and SPEC.md's Context section. The full pipeline runs; when the PR opens, Jira moves to In Review. No Jira comments or field edits are made. If Jira is unavailable (no Atlassian MCP, or the issue can't be read), it proceeds treating the key as a free-form task, records that, and reports Jira as skipped instead of failing.
expectations: WORK_LOG.md's Ticket line carries JIRA-1234
With Jira available: the In Progress transition happens only after the user confirms it
No Jira comment or field-edit tool is called — transitions only
With Jira unavailable: the run continues past Phase 1 and the report says Jira was skipped

evals.prompt: auto-dev this whole epic: add multi-currency support across the wallet, the ledger, and the payout service. Take it all the way.
evals.expected_output: Phase 2's auto-dev:define writes SPEC.md and returns SIZE: OVERSIZED, with its reasons, the subsystems it found (the wallet, the ledger and the payout service, each with a rough file count) and suggested lines to split along. The orchestrator records Size: OVERSIZED in WORK_LOG.md's header, marks Phase 2 blocked with the Notes OVERSIZED and Phases 3-6 n/a, and stops. It does not spawn the Define reviewer or any later worker, writes no code, creates no sub-tasks, second worktree or branch, and asks no approval to split the task. No Jira transition is attempted. The worktree and branch from Phase 1 are left in place. Its final message tells the user the task is too big for one PR, gives Define's reasons, subsystems and suggested split lines, names SPEC.md's path, and gives the commands that remove the worktree and branch (`git worktree remove <worktree>`, `git branch -D <branch>`).
expectations: WORK_LOG.md's header records Size: OVERSIZED; Phase 2 is blocked with Notes OVERSIZED and Phases 3-6 are n/a
No define-reviewer, planner, plan-reviewer, acceptance-tester or coder agent is spawned, and no source file changes
WORK_LOG.md has no Sub-tasks table, `git worktree list` shows only the main checkout and the run's one worktree, and the user is not asked to approve a breakdown
No Jira transition is attempted
The final message says the task is too big for one PR and gives the reasons, the subsystems found and suggested split lines
The worktree and branch still exist, and the final message gives the commands to remove them

evals.prompt: auto-dev: the error message on the expiry validation says 'invalid date' — make it say which field was invalid. Ship it.
evals.expected_output: A one-file, one-behavior change runs the same steps as any other task. The workers are auto-dev:define, auto-dev:define-reviewer, auto-dev:planner, auto-dev:plan-reviewer, auto-dev:acceptance-tester, auto-dev:coder, auto-dev:verifier, auto-dev:cleanup and, in S3, the three code reviewers, the review judge and the security reviewer; read-and-answer lookups via auto-dev:lookup don't count against that. SPEC.md and IMPLEMENTATION.md are the only documents describing the work before code, and the planner writes IMPLEMENTATION.md (profile.md and WORK_LOG.md also exist from Phase 1, as setup state and the ledger). Verify and Ship are not thinned: SPEC_EVAL.md, one lint/*.md per gate command, CODE_REVIEW.md and SECURITY_REVIEW.md are all produced, and the run still pauses at the PR gate. If the orchestrator skips a planning step or writes the plan itself because the task is small, the one-workflow rule is not working.
expectations: WORK_LOG.md's header records Size: FITS
auto-dev:define-reviewer, auto-dev:planner and auto-dev:plan-reviewer are each spawned, and auto-dev:planner writes IMPLEMENTATION.md
The only .auto-dev/ files before the coder runs are profile.md, WORK_LOG.md, SPEC.md, IMPLEMENTATION.md, HANDOFF.md and acceptance/ (plus .gitignore and an empty lint/)
The changed error message names the invalid field, and a test asserts the new message
SPEC_EVAL.md and lint/*.md exist after S2 — verification is not skipped

evals.setup: Run eval 1's S1 to completion (or build the equivalent state by hand): the run's worktree with SPEC.md, IMPLEMENTATION.md, acceptance/ (MANIFEST.md and the sealed files/), profile.md, and the WORK_LOG.md and HANDOFF.md in files/ (edit their paths to the real worktree). Start a fresh session in the main repo checkout, not the worktree.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator finds the run without being told where: it scans `git worktree list` and runs scripts/resume-point.py on each candidate's .auto-dev/, which reports Phase 4 — Build as the first open phase, in S2. It does not re-run Phase 1 or re-resolve the profile. On entry it reads WORK_LOG.md, HANDOFF.md and profile.md and nothing else by default; it copies the S2 checklist into TodoWrite. It spawns auto-dev:coder with IMPLEMENTATION.md only (the size check was FITS), marks Phase 4 in-progress before starting it, then spawns auto-dev:verifier for Phase 5 (it installs the sealed checks; the orchestrator reads SPEC_EVAL.md, not the diff) and stops at the S2 boundary with a Ship-brief HANDOFF.md naming sonnet/medium.
expectations: scripts/resume-point.py is run against the run's worktree's .auto-dev/ before any phase work
No Phase 1 step re-runs: no new worktree, no profile re-detection, and profile.md is not rewritten
Before spawning the coder, the orchestrator reads no .auto-dev/ file other than WORK_LOG.md, HANDOFF.md and profile.md
WORK_LOG.md marks Phase 4 in-progress before the coder is spawned
The session ends with HANDOFF.md naming Phase 6 next and telling the user to start a fresh session on sonnet at medium effort

evals.setup: Run eval 1 through Phase 4, then plant a defect the spec catches (e.g. the guard accepts an out-of-set value in one context). Set the ledger's iteration budget to `4 total revise rounds (0 remaining)` and Phase 5 to in-progress, as in files/.
evals.expected_output: Phase 5 re-runs whole. The verifier finds the unmet condition (its acceptance check fails) and writes it in SPEC_EVAL.md, but with zero rounds left the correction loop does not run: no coder is spawned. The orchestrator stops and reports which loop ran the budget out, each unmet condition by name (not a summary), and what was tried, and leaves the work in place. It does not go on to /simplify, the quality gate or Phase 6, and it does not report success.
expectations: SPEC_EVAL.md, written by auto-dev:verifier, marks the planted condition partial or unmet, with evidence it ran
No auto-dev:coder is spawned in this session
The final message names each unmet condition and says the iteration budget is exhausted
The cleanup agent is not spawned, and nothing is committed or pushed
WORK_LOG.md records the stop and the remaining budget as 0

evals.setup: Run eval 5 through S2 in a fixture repo with no CI config (profile.md records `CI provider: none`), as in files/. Run interactively so the PR gate can be approved; decline the main gate.
evals.expected_output: S3 reads WORK_LOG.md, HANDOFF.md and profile.md, then SPEC.md, SPEC_EVAL.md, lint/*.md, acceptance/MANIFEST.md, acceptance/base-run/C<n>.txt and evidence/C<n>.txt for the PR body. It runs the code review panel and the security review first (CODE_REVIEW.md, SECURITY_REVIEW.md), then pauses at the PR gate; on approval it stages explicit paths (deleted paths via `git rm --cached`), passes scripts/check-staged.py --expect, commits, pushes without --force, and opens one draft PR with `gh pr create --base <base> --title … --body-file … --draft` (or a fitting PR skill that meets the same requirements). Because the CI provider is `none` it skips the CI watch entirely and records that; it does not poll `gh pr checks` or treat 'no checks reported' as red. The staging gate is n/a. Before the main gate it fetches the PR branch and runs scripts/check-fresh.py --ref origin/<branch>, which exits 0 (nobody else pushed), and the gate summary names the PR's head commit as the one every result checked. At the main gate it is declined: it stops with the PR open, without merging or moving Jira.
expectations: The PR is a draft against the base branch, and exactly one PR exists for the branch
scripts/check-staged.py exits 0 before the commit, and nothing under .auto-dev/ is committed

CODE_REVIEW.md is written by the auto-dev:review-judge agent from three auto-dev:code-reviewer reports, and SECURITY_REVIEW.md by auto-dev:security-reviewer (or security-reviewer-sensitive), both before the PR gate
No CI watch runs (no `gh pr checks --watch` or polling loop), and WORK_LOG.md records that CI was skipped because the provider is none
Before the main gate is asked, the PR branch is fetched and scripts/check-fresh.py --ref origin/<branch> exits 0
After the main gate is declined, no `gh pr merge` is run and the PR stays open

evals.setup: Run eval 5 through S2, then start S3 on a repo with CI. Let the code review panel finish (CODE_REVIEW.md written, the Phase 6 Notes recording `code review pass 1: done, 0 open`), then interrupt the session while the security reviewer is writing SECURITY_REVIEW.md, before the PR gate, and leave SECURITY_REVIEW.md truncated. Put the WORK_LOG.md in files/ (Phase 6 in-progress) in the run's worktree, delete HANDOFF.md, and start a fresh session in the main repo checkout. Run interactively, approve the PR gate and decline the main gate.
evals.expected_output: resume-point.py reports Phase 6 — Ship, status in-progress, in S3, with the Phase 6 Action (reconcile, then continue after the last gate passed, re-running any review step the Notes don't record as done) and no `Note:` line. The orchestrator does not re-run Phase 6 whole: it checks git log, git status, the remote branch and gh pr view, finds no commit and no PR, and so knows no gate has passed and the run was in the reviews. The Notes record the code review as done, so it does not re-spawn the code review panel. It does not trust the truncated SECURITY_REVIEW.md: it re-spawns the security reviewer, which re-writes it in full. Then it asks the PR gate, commits, pushes and opens exactly one PR, watches CI, and at the main gate it is declined: it stops with the PR open.
expectations: scripts/resume-point.py is run before any Phase 6 work, and its Action for Phase 6 in-progress is followed rather than re-running the phase whole
git log / gh pr view (or equivalent) is checked before acting, and finding no commit or PR, the run resumes in the reviews rather than at a later step
No auto-dev:code-reviewer agent is spawned again for pass 1, because the Notes record that pass as done
SECURITY_REVIEW.md is re-written in full by the auto-dev:security-reviewer (or security-reviewer-sensitive) agent before the PR gate is asked
Exactly one PR exists for the branch afterwards, and after the main gate is declined, no `gh pr merge` is run and the PR stays open

evals.setup: Run eval 1 through Phase 4 (S1 leaves acceptance/ sealed; leave it so). Then, in the worktree, delete the assertion from one pre-existing test the change does not touch, and mark another as skipped with the test framework's own marker (for example `it.skip`; example in TypeScript). Set Phase 4 done and Phase 5 pending in the ledger from files/, with at least 2 rounds remaining.
evals.expected_output: Phase 5 starts with the verifier. scripts/check-tests.py reports REMOVED_ASSERTION and ADDED_SKIP on the planted tests (exit 1); no SPEC.md condition changes that behavior, so the verifier judges both Unjustified in SPEC_EVAL.md's Test integrity section. The orchestrator treats them as a Phase 5 correction: one brief to auto-dev:coder, spending one round, naming which tests to restore, then a verifier re-check finds the audit clean of those findings. The cleanup agent runs only after that. The planted edits never reach a PR.
expectations: SPEC_EVAL.md's Test integrity section lists the removed assertion and the added skip, each judged Unjustified
A correction brief to auto-dev:coder names both tests to restore, and WORK_LOG.md shows one round spent for it
A second verifier pass runs after the correction, and its SPEC_EVAL.md no longer lists either finding
The cleanup agent is spawned only after the verifier's audit is clean of unjustified findings
No condition is marked met while an unjustified integrity finding touches it

evals.setup: Run eval 1 through Phase 4, then delete the test that covers the boundary of the allowed set (e.g. the first or last allowed value is accepted) while keeping the acceptance checks sealed and the rest of the suite green. Set Phase 4 done and Phase 5 pending in the ledger from files/, with at least 2 rounds remaining.
evals.expected_output: The verifier's mutation step plants a boundary mutant on the guard (e.g. the membership check made to reject the edge value) and no test fails, so the mutant survives. The verifier judges it a Test gap on the condition's line, marks that condition partial and lists the survivor in SPEC_EVAL.md's Mutation section. The orchestrator sends one correction describing the behavior to pin (the edge value is accepted), never the mutant itself; the coder adds that test; the verifier's re-check re-runs the survivor and it is now killed. The source is unchanged by the mutation runs throughout.
expectations: evidence/mutants.json holds only mutants on changed source lines, each tagged with a condition
SPEC_EVAL.md lists the surviving boundary mutant as a Test gap and marks its condition partial
The correction brief describes the unpinned behavior in plain words and does not quote the mutant's find/replace
The re-check re-runs that mutant and records it killed; the condition is then met
git diff origin/<base> after each verifier pass contains no mutant, and no mutants.json.backup directory remains

evals.setup: Point AUTO_DEV_PROFILES_DIR at an empty throwaway directory, and make sure the fixture repo has no .auto-dev.yml. Run interactively so the profile confirmation can be answered: first answer `Change something` and ask for one gate command to be dropped, then answer `Looks right — save it for this repo`. Stop the run at the first pause after Phase 1.
evals.prompt: Auto-dev this: reject creation of a record when the requested value isn't in the allowed set for that context. Take it all the way to a PR.
evals.expected_output: Phase 1 checks gh, then runs scripts/profile-path.py on the main checkout, which prints NOT FOUND with a path under AUTO_DEV_PROFILES_DIR (exit 1). The orchestrator spawns auto-dev:profiler (its agent type, no model parameter) on the main checkout, before any worktree exists; the profiler writes nothing and returns PROFILE, EVIDENCE, NOT ADOPTED, NOT INSTALLED and QUESTIONS. The orchestrator pauses with AskUserQuestion: the summary shows the draft YAML, an evidence line per command, the profiler's questions, the save path, and the permissions guidance with Read and Edit rules for the profiles directory and Bash rules for this run's commands, and the options are save / this run only / change something / stop. After `Change something` it drops the named check itself and asks again, spending no iteration-budget round. After the save answer it writes the confirmed profile to the printed path, validates it with scripts/validate-config.py --profile (exit 0), and continues to the worktree with the confirmed commands. It never edits a Claude Code settings file.
expectations: auto-dev:profiler is spawned before `git worktree add`, and git status in the main checkout is unchanged after it returns
The confirmation summary carries the save path and a permissions snippet with Read(...) and Edit(...) rules for the profiles directory and Bash(...) rules naming this run's setup and gate commands
The dropped check is absent from the second confirmation, from the saved file and from profile.md's quality gate; WORK_LOG.md's budget is unchanged by the change
The saved file exists at the path profile-path.py printed, holds only profile keys (stack, setup, gate, test_notes, worktree_files, symbol_lookup, ci) and passes validate-config.py --profile
profile.md's Profile line reads researched, confirmed, saved to that path
No file under ~/.claude/ or any .claude/settings*.json is written

evals.session: S1 (saved profile reused, then a broken one)
evals.setup: Run eval 13 first, so a saved profile exists for the fixture repo under AUTO_DEV_PROFILES_DIR. Then make a fresh clone of the fixture repo in a different directory and start the session there. For the second run, replace the saved file's contents with a profile that sets only `setup` (keep its setup list, delete `gate`) and start again from that clone, interactively.
evals.prompt: Auto-dev this: add a configurable limit to the number of records a single request may create. Take it all the way to a PR.
evals.expected_output: First run: scripts/profile-path.py on the new clone prints FOUND with the same path eval 13 saved to (exit 0), since the path comes from the origin remote rather than the checkout's directory.
